releaseNotes: Platform release: a deliverable's version history now says what each version changed. Formation has always kept every version, which is the right thing to keep and, on its own, not much use — a founder looking at version seven could see that six earlier ones existed and could not see what any of them did. Each row now carries one sentence on the closed row ("1 section rewritten, 1 added", "Status draft → reviewed", "Confidence rose from 60% to 82%") and the specifics when opened, including which sections were revised and by how many words.

The summary is computed from the immutable versions rather than written when one is saved. A note written at save time is a claim about the change, and it can drift from the record it describes — which matters more here than usual, because a change summary will be believed. Sections are matched by their own ids first, so an edit reads as an edit rather than as one section removed and another added; where an id is missing the title is the fallback and only then position, and position is refused when both sides carry ids that differ, since a different id is positive evidence that two sections are not the same section. The earliest version a store still retains does not claim to have been the first one written. Checks, 186 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
